Tech Report: You Know Animal-Print Rugs, But Do You Know Animal Pictorials? (2026)

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1392 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the oldest known pile rug—pulled from a frozen tomb in Siberia in 1949—features a procession of 24 fallow deer and a parade of men on horseback.
  • According to recent reports, rajaram is describing a literal animal rug, also known as an animal pictorial.
  • “What we’re seeing now is a shift toward rugs where the whole animal is part of the design and has a role in the composition,” notes Kerri Anne Besse, design director at rug brand Tumble.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the oldest known pile rug—pulled from a frozen tomb in Siberia in 1949—features a procession of 24 fallow deer and a parade of men on horseback. Some 2,500 years after its creation, animal illustrations are making their way back onto the floor. A serpent coils through the Snake and Pomegranate rug by Christopher Farr and Studio Shamshiri in Lucy Hale’s Los Angeles home, and a Tibetan tiger stretches across Demi Lovato’s modern farmhouse and Ethan Cook’s SoHo loft. These aren’t spots or stripes standing in for a neutral—they’re meant to be noticed and discussed. “Animal print is a texture; an animal motif is a story,” states AD100 designer Pavitra Rajaram, who recently designed Bahaar, an animal-themed rug in her Majnun collection for Jaipur Living. “I think people are tired of decoration that says nothing and are looking for objects that carry meaning.”.

According to recent reports, rajaram is describing a literal animal rug, also known as an animal pictorial. These playful floor coverings often feature a bucolic scene of several animals or a single animal form woven into the textile, and they come in styles ranging from avant-garde and surrealist to Art Deco and folk-inspired.

A master bedroom by Studio Duggan.

“What we’re seeing now is a shift toward rugs where the whole animal is part of the design and has a role in the composition,” notes Kerri Anne Besse, design director at rug brand Tumble. “The oversized, blown-up animal print feels dated.”.

As for styling, Sophie Salata, head of brand at Vinterior, recommends that designers let the pictorials stand on their own. “I’d be inclined to treat the rug almost as a piece of art, allowing it to become a focal point rather than trying to make everything around it match,” she claims. Pamela Marshall, creative director at artisanal rug brand Patterson Flynn, agrees with this approach: These designs are more than backdrops.

Reformation's nine-piece rug collection with Les Éditions de Tapis includes depictions of cats, swans, and tigers.

Recently, brands have been launching their own interpretations of animal pictorials. Last week, Reformation launched its first-ever home collection, a collaboration with Les Éditions de Tapis that features hand-drawn swans and cats. At Milan Design Week this year, Fornasetti launched a surrealist-inspired line of rugs with CC-Tapis depicting slithering serpents from the luxury designer’s archive. A few months earlier, Ruggable released its collaboration with Scalamandré to bring the upscale design house’s iconic zebras to more homes. And in October 2025, Nordic Knots launched its Swedish Grace collection, including the Grace 03 Fauna rug, which shows a wildlife scene. Looking further back, Beni’s serpent rugs have been a designer favorite since 2020.

One of the earlier examples of literal animal rugs is a collection between longstanding collaborators Patterson Flynn and AD100 designers Charlap Hyman & Herrero. It grew from a one-off rug into a full collection of graphic natural-and-black silhouettes that launched in 2018 and continues to expand. “Areas of inspiration for these come from Calder’s simplified animal forms, the surrealists’ play on scale, and 17th-century cabinets of curiosity, to name a few,” notes Marshall, who credits Hyman’s “encyclopedic” design references for the originality. We would be remiss not to mention Diane von Furstenberg’s long-running collaboration with the Rug Company, which has been producing the iconic Climbing Leopard rug since 2005.

Rugs from Charlap Hyman & Herrero x Patterson Flynn’s collaboration.

The Rug Firm x Diane von Furstenberg Climbing Leopard rug in emerald.

These rugs’ rich history might be part of their renewed appeal. Animals have been a subject for as long as people have made pictures. The oldest known figurative cave painting—found in Indonesia and dated to at least 51,200 years ago—highlights a wild pig with three human figures.

According to recent reports, “Animals have shaped our textiles and rugs for longer than we think,” indicates Bella Valenzia, founder of Pelican House, pointing out that animal forms have appeared in tapestries and wall coverings, and as functional home objects, such as pelt and hide rugs used for warmth and comfort, since the earliest days of humankind. “We like to think it is part of a wider return to folk-inspired, storytelling textiles, with a sense of nostalgia,” she adds. Pelican House’s rug Frith references the old English countryside, where horses have long been at the heart of rural life.

According to recent reports, various animals, real and mythical, carry their own significance across cultures, and their meaning can deeply influence a home’s design. For example, a pictorial of a lion, which signifies power in certain cultures, adds a very different element to a space than a fish, which can signify good luck, notes Jahanshah “Josh” Nazmiyal of Rug & Kilim. Veronica Renton, senior vintage and antiques specialist at 1stDibs, adds that peacocks often signal nobility and immortality.

Plenty of designers still reach for the originals: While the contemporary versions of these rugs are having a moment, their earlier counterparts remain relevant. “I particularly love antique Tibetan tiger rugs and Persian and Chinese rugs featuring guardian lions, dragons, and all manner of mythical beasts,” indicates Tiffany Duggan, founder of Studio Duggan.

The Tiger Rug by Studio Ashby in Sophie Ashby’s former home in London.

Where these rugs live in the home is likewise crucial. Naturally, the pieces work well in spaces that are meant to be playful, like nurseries and children’s rooms. For example, in this garden apartment designed by Rebecca Benichou and Florence Jallet of Batiik Studio, the Toulemonde Bochart Lion rug brings a spot of levity to a windowless craft room. In the bedroom of Kate Upton and Justin Verlander’s daughter, Genevieve, designed by John Ruggiero, the Doing Goods Blooming Black Bear Rug provides a spot of whimsy. For double the fun, designer Olivia Song put two animal rugs, the Doing Goods Pinky Lion and Pinky Leopard, in her nephew’s room in this Sag Harbor beach home.

That said, these rugs work in more adult spaces, too. “In the [primary] bedroom of one of our London projects, we used the beautiful Snake and Pomegranate rug,” indicates Duggan. “I love the way the snake weaves its way around the bed, creating a focal point and bringing a little humor and unexpected character to an otherwise calm space.”.

Designer Rayman Boozer from Apartment 48 has a rug with a large tiger on it from the Rug Firm in his own home. “Animal motifs can sometimes feel juvenile, but there’s something refreshing about bringing that sense of playfulness into a sophisticated space,” he indicates.

Rayman Boozer’s home, featuring an Apartment 48 tiger rug.

Sources indicate that steven Loloi, co-principal at Loloi, agrees. Speaking of Loloi’s Roam collection that launched last month and features cheetahs, zebras, elephants, and giraffes in neutral colors, he highlights the surprising versatility of the pieces, which he says can fit just as nicely in a bedroom or living room as in a lounge or den. “I think we’re seeing people become more confident in their design choices and a little less concerned with playing it safe,” he says. “Why not have a leopard or zebra in your living room?”.

Industry observers note that it’s worth noting that these rugs aren’t for everyone, and some designers avoid any type of animal rug because of the hunting culture they reference. Others, though, embrace them as a way to reimagine humanity’s relationship to animals and commit to living better by them.

Recent findings suggest that rajaram's Bahaar rug does just that with its contemporary expression of 'shikargahs,' the enclosed forests where kings hunted at leisure, which are celebrated in Iranian and Mughal design. “Instead of being chased, the animals are in harmony with each other, frolicking freely in the forest. It’s a celebration of coexistence rather than conquest,” she states. The Charlap Hyman & Herrero x Patterson Flynn collection had a similar ambition: “Our Tigre and Oso nod to traditional hide floor coverings; they give you the drama of the trophy rug without the trophy,” notes Marshall.

In a recent development, on the surface, the return of these animal-forward rugs might have looked like a change in aesthetics, but it’s really much more anthropological. “We have always gravitated toward pieces with animals, and even in modern production, history is repeating itself,” indicates Nazmiyal. Some 2,500 years after their first spotting, these animal-clad rugs are back home.

Industry News: RFK Jr.’s Revised Vaccine Schedule May Cause 83% Surge in Hepatitis B Infections

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F.
  • Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.
  • A new study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s proposed changes to the childhood vaccine schedule have raised alarm among public health experts and researchers.

Concerns include a rise in preventable infectious diseases such as measles, polio, and hepatitis B.

A new study suggests that delaying or foregoing the hepatitis B shot for newborns could increase chronic infections among children.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) ended its recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for the virus. Instead, the federal health agency recommends individual-based clinical decision making.

After reviewing the evidence, the CDC, which is overseen by the HHS, concluded that newborns “face little risk of contracting hepatitis,” which deemed the vaccine, typically administered at birth, unnecessary.

Experts say this shift in public health policy wasn’t based on science, and researchers warn of rising infection rates.

“Hepatitis B immunizations have been proven to protect individuals against a serious and significant disease,” stated Graham Tse, MD, pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

According to recent reports, “The hepatitis B vaccines have several decades of history and have been proven safe and effective,” Tse said. “There has been no new data or evidence presented or uncovered to support delaying the newborn dose of hepatitis B.”.

Here’s what parents should know about making informed decisions with their child’s healthcare team.

It has been revealed that A U.S. modeling study published in Annals of Internal Medicine on October 20 projected that delaying the first vaccine dose until 2 months could increase chronic hepatitis B infections among infants by 19% under one scenario.

With shared decision making and lower vaccine uptake, projected increases ranged from 83% to 225%, compared with universal birth-dose vaccination.

The researchers also estimated that up to 1.8 million young adults could remain susceptible to hepatitis B by age 20 under shared decision making, compared with 232,000 under universal birth dosing.

Another study published in JAMA Pediatrics in late April projected hundreds of additional chronic infections annually if the hepatitis B birth dose were delayed or omitted.

However, these figures are model-based projections, rather than verified outcomes. Actual results will depend on vaccination rates and other factors.

In December 2025, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) adopted a recommendation shifting away from universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth for infants whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).

Under the newly introduced approach, parents and healthcare professionals can decide together whether to give the first dose at birth or defer it until the baby is 2 months old.

According to recent reports, the change followed an 8 to 3 vote by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), marking a departure from longstanding U.S. guidance.

However, infants born to mothers who test positive for hepatitis B or whose infection status is unknown should still receive the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin (HBIG) within 12 hours of birth, according to the updated guidelines.

Hepatitis B is a viral infection that affects the liver.

Although some infections resolve, newborns and infants face a higher risk of developing lifelong hepatitis B infection compared with adults.

Up to 90% of infants infected during their first year develop chronic hepatitis B.

“We have actual world evidence that vaccinating newborns for hepatitis B prevents hepatitis B infections later in life and the serious complications of that disease,” Tse said.

Over time, chronic infection can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, or liver cancer.

“The danger of delaying the newborn hepatitis B shot is that individuals do not get vaccinated and thereby do not have protection against hepatitis B,” Tse mentioned.

Early vaccination helps protect young infants before potential exposure occurs, including situations in which maternal screening misses an infection.

“Newborns can be infected with hepatitis B from a mother who is not aware they have a hepatitis B infection or from exposure later in life,” Tse remarked.

“The risk is developing a hepatitis B infection, which can potentially lead to liver cancer, fulminant hepatitis, or severe end-stage liver disease.”.

In contrast to the CDC, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) still recommends a universal hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth, followed by additional doses during infancy.

The leading pediatric medical organization has raised concerns about the potential consequences of reduced vaccination rates.

The hepatitis B vaccine has decades of safety and effectiveness data.

Tse said the AAP’s vaccine schedule and recommendations are based on decades of study, use, and expert input, and provide the best protection against vaccine-preventable diseases.

Parents who have questions about potential side effects, timing, or their baby’s individual risk should discuss them with a qualified healthcare professional.

“Parents are confused, given the recommendations from CDC, HHS, and Kennedy differ from established and respected groups such as the American Academy of Pediatrics, the Infectious Disease Society of America, and several states,” Tse said.

“Parents desire to keep their children safe, and having differing opinions and confusion will lead to reduced vaccination rates as parents experience doubt as to whom to listen to or believe.”.

While the updated CDC policy offers more flexibility for some families, lower vaccination uptake could lead to an increase in chronic hepatitis B infections.

Ask your pediatrician about the benefits of vaccination against hepatitis B at birth, the risks of delaying the first dose, and the recommended schedule for completing the series.

You can also ask how maternal screening results affect your baby’s protection.

An informed conversation with your healthcare professional can help you weigh the evidence and choose a vaccination initiative for your baby.

“I see no argument whatsoever for changing the established vaccination schedule for hepatitis B,” Tse noted.

According to recent reports, “There have been no new studies, no data, nor evidence to justify Kennedy’s proposed changes to the childhood immunization schedule. Delaying vaccinations or skipping vaccinations puts your child at risk for serious and significant diseases, which are all preventable,” Tse noted.

Shadow welcomes unknown female bald eagle to his nest

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (794 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Internet-famous bald eagle Shadow has endured an up-and-down 2026.
  • Industry observers note that after the August death of Jackie, the female eagle he raised chicks with since 2018, Shadow began spending time with a 4-year-old female eagle named Kaydee (formerly KD1).
  • It has been revealed that cameras spotted the unknown female in the nest in recent weeks, but this was the first time the eagle was joined by Shadow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Internet-famous bald eagle Shadow has endured an up-and-down 2026. From suffering the loss of a clutch of eggs to welcoming two chicks, and from losing his longtime partner to finding a new friend, he’s had a tumultuous year.

Industry observers note that after the August death of Jackie, the female eagle he raised chicks with since 2018, Shadow began spending time with a 4-year-old female eagle named Kaydee (formerly KD1). Viewers of the 24/7 livestream of Shadow’s nest could easily spot Kaydee because of her double-banded legs—a silver ring on one leg and a lavender one on the other. The pair appeared chummy as they spent more time together, sharing stick-arranging duties, singing, and exchanging beaky kisses. An unexpected twist arrived this week with the appearance of an unknown female bald eagle spotted in the nest with Shadow.

It has been revealed that cameras spotted the unknown female in the nest in recent weeks, but this was the first time the eagle was joined by Shadow. On Monday afternoon, Shadow landed in the nest swiftly followed by the unknown female. The unknown female fiddled the nest sticks while vocalizing and Shadow appeared unbothered by her presence. Eagles will typically defend their nest from intruders so Shadow’s willingness to share his space with an eagle other than Kaydee surprised many viewers.

Shadow returned the nest solo later in the afternoon as the sun set over Big Bear Lake.

Industry observers note that as this is nature, all we can do is sit back and see what unfolds. Mating season is approaching, so we have to wait and see if Shadow selects a latest partner. Female eagles in Major Bear Valley typically lay their first clutch of eggs in January. Tune in to Friends of Big Bear Valley’s (FOBBV) livestreams to follow the southern California eagles anytime.

Kaydee, formerly known as KD1, is a banded female bald eagle that has been spotted in Significant Bear Valley following the death of Shadow’s former partner, Jackie. She was born in 2022, about 70 miles away from Big Bear Lake in the Prado Basin between Anaheim and Riverside, California. Coincidentally, her parents are also named Lucky and Ricky like Jackie’s parents, but they are a different eagle pair.

It has been revealed that kaydee was banded as part of the Orange County Water District’s work to track the eagles born in the area. These bands help biologists track and monitor the birds over time. Kaydee right now has a black spot on her head, but it may not be permanent. It’s possible that not all of her white feathers have come in or it could be tree sap or dirt. She also has two small bands on her legs. One is a small metal band, while the other is a lavender band with “KD1” on it.

Kaydee is almost five years old, so she is just about ready to mate. She was recently spotted on FOBBV’s livestream inspecting the nest and has also been seen hanging out near Shadow. Flying around Significant Bear is completely normal behavior for young adult eagles at this time of year.

It has been revealed that in January, Jackie laid two eggs in the nest, but ravens destroyed them. She later laid two more eggs that hatched in April and named Luna and Sandy. The name Sandy is in honor of FOBBV’s former executive director Sandy Steers who died from cancer in February.

Recent findings suggest that on July 17, Jackie was found injured on the ground near Dana Point Park, California. Cell phone video from a witness confirmed that she had an altercation with two other subadult eagles. She successfully fended off the other eagles by turning over and using her talons, but could not fly far away.

In a recent development, she was transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for care, where she was diagnosed with severe anemia. Her anemia worsened during the first week of August, the Ojai Raptor Center mentioned that she was in unstable condition on August 9. Her packed cell volume (PCV) fell below six percent, before rising to nine percent. Jackie died early in the morning on August 10. The necropsy did not reveal a single cause of death, and instead pointed to several factors including severe anemia, bird flu, blood clots in her wing and one kidney, and liver and lung abnormalities.

In a recent development, A memorial service was held on September 5 in Fawnskin, California, along with a second celebration of life called Wings Over Big Bear on October 3. The event featured representatives from FOBBV, the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, and more.

It has been revealed that IF YOU’RE JUST getting into golf, there will be a time in your life when you need to invest in a golf club set. As it’s a lifetime pursuit, it’s best to invest in a decent setup, and if well maintained, it can last you for years to come. While advanced players may want to customize their own golf club sets, there are numerous brands that make complete sets that will have you playing from day one. Even notable brands like Callaway and Wilson have solid options.

It's true you could go buy pre-owned clubs as your first beginner set, which is not a bad idea to peruse your local Dick's Sporting Goods or local golf shop (especially for previous year model demos during the offseason), brand sites' used portals like Callaway Certified Pre-Owned, or eBay. But if you've gotten the golf bug and are looking for a fresh-to-you set, these days golf brands are churning out shiny, high-quality sets at affordable entry points. Customization is also better than ever, as several outfitters offer club length adjustments, different club combinations, and a selection of stylish golf bags to accompany them. You can always ask for a set as a great golf gift, too.

Whichever route you choose, we spoke with Paul Silva, head pro at NYC’s Van Cortlandt Golf Club to answer some of the most frequently asked questions when it comes to buying a beginner golf set. After you get a legit set, don't forget about some golf shoes.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to the game of golf, not many brands can boast expertise in every single category. One that can though is Callaway. The brand behind elite golf balls, top-tier putters, golf bags, pro-worthy irons and drivers, Callaway is no slouch when it comes to making high-quality gear for beginners.

The 2026 XR lineup comes in a 13-piece set, which includes a mallet putter made by Odyssey and its DFX V-line Fang shape, which offers higher stability and more aggressive alignment aids—two elements you’re rarely going to find in an entry-level putter. The irons are classics, based on decades of stellar game-improvement technology, while the hybrids, 3-wood, and driver are modeled after one of golf’s most exciting upcoming weapons of the past couple of years, the Paradym. This year you also get an approach wedge. Add on the fact of its high-MOI V-Line putter and you get a set that dominates the short game. This set will set you back more than most, but don’t be surprised if you tote these clubs along with you for the next ten years.Read More: The Best Golf Shirts.

Though technically a slightly older legacy bundle, this platinum set features two premium features we love. The first is the irons. They're well-built and just what you want out of a beginner iron, making them a solid set to build the base of your arsenal for years to come. Considered a game improvement set, they have a thinner top line and are more refined. The second is the golf bag: It's highly comfortable thanks to the dual carrying strap and lightweight design, and comes with ample pocket space.

Wilson is a brand with immense golf pedigree—no player worth their salt will scoff at the brand’s gear, whether you’re shooting even par or 20-over. The set is immensely affordable, so while it will probably long outlast your golf career, it won’t make you feel bad about upgrading once you start to improve.

Read More: Best Golf Clubs on Amazon.

Industry observers note that for someone just getting into the game or hitting the range for the very first time, this set is great to start with. With every club you’ll need to get from the tee box to the green (and probably everywhere in between), this set won’t leave you without an option, no matter how wayward your shots get.

It has been revealed that the set has a solid 4.3-out-of-5-star rating on Amazon, with reviewers lauding the set’s value and high level of forgiveness. Odds are high you’ll want to upgrade sooner than later, but if you or someone you know likes to pick up upcoming hobbies, this set will help decide if golf is a lifelong commitment or just a phase.

While one of the most expensive of the bunch, this TaylorMade set is certifiably legit. We're talking about a beast of a driver which features an adjustable driver, allowing you to change the loft and face angle as your swing evolves (something you hardly ever find on a complete set driver), a beautiful set of high-performance irons, and a stylish golf bag that will protect your investment with reassurance.

This is a set for those who are getting serious and playing several times per week. The barrier to entry is higher than the rest of the options on our list, but when you consider the pedigree of a brand like TaylorMade, you’ll find that the long lifespan of the clubs and golf bag make it a set you can grow into and not have to replace for years.

Picking up on the game quicker than you thought? You can skip the early stages and go for a complete set that allows you to learn how to optimize your shot-making skills. The Stix Perform Set is a complete 12-club set that will provide you with all the tools you need, all for under $1,000.

Industry observers note that the Perform Set is the brand’s first set with the option for irons with a steel shaft, a boon for mid-high handicap players whose higher swing speeds may be a bit too much for the extra flex of graphite. Clubs that benefit from the flex (the driver, 3 wood, and 4 hybrid) still come standard with graphite, but having the choice when selecting irons is going to greatly increase the amount of time you’ll stick with your Stix.

In my testing, I took the Stix out for a couple dozen rounds, walking and riding in a cart. The set is very manageable size-wise. The bag is light enough for comfortable wear but big enough to stay secure when strapped to the back of a golf cart. They’re some of the most forgiving clubs I've played and are well-built, resulting in improved distance and fewer mishits. My favorite club was the 4 iron hybrid—I've never hit a hybrid so well.

Sources indicate that another set from one of the most prestigious equipment brands in golf, the Cobra Fly XL set is the ideal set for someone who knows they’re going to be consistently hitting the golf course in a golf cart. The cart bag is big, sturdy, and spacious, while the wide range of clubs gives you options in every part of the course.

Industry observers note that the Cobra brand is well-recognized, and these striking clubs will fit in with any other sets on the course, ensuring that your skills do the talking, not your equipment. If your skills are lacking, that’s okay, too, because each club in this set is super forgiving thanks to excellent weight distribution and optimized shape, from the driver right down through the putter.

When you’re looking for a little more performance but still trying to stay affordable, PXG is a brand to look to. This Wildcat Bundle is an extremely versatile setup that utilizes premium materials and the same tech found in the brand’s standalone clubs, all tuned for maximum forgiveness and easy launch—must-haves for beginners.

In a recent development, while it is a hefty investment, they’re the one-and-done purchase type, meaning that you won’t outgrow them anytime soon, and will last for years to come. These clubs are meant to bridge the gap from significant box store generic clubs and a custom-fitted pro set, while providing a fairway-friendly driver and the brand’s polymer cores for a softer feel and more distance. While it’s only a 9-club set, it has all the essentials you’ll need to make it up and down on any course.

It has been revealed that most beginner sets will include between nine and 11 clubs. 10 is a good sweet spot; it is enough to have a driver, a fairway wood and/or a hybrid, a 5i-9i, a wedge, and a putter. Generally a full set is 14 clubs; that includes the putter—and you can keep no more than that number in your bag during play.

In a recent development, two recommendations we would make would be to forego a 3-wood in favor of a 5-wood or 4-hybrid—most players don’t actually need a 3-wood and would be better served with a more forgiving hybrid (or two). If you can, consider adding a sand wedge (or potentially a lob wedge that you learn how to use) to sit alongside your pitching wedge, as many pitching wedges aren’t lofted enough for tricky shots in the sand or around the greens.

Sources indicate that as Silva told us, "I tell everyone the same thing in the beginning, find a few clubs that you can hit—a hybrid, a 5 iron, a 7 iron, a pitching wedge, a putter. You can learn to do a lot with those things, especially in the beginning. You don’t need to worry so much about distance.".

Sources indicate that most beginners will want a shaft made of graphite. These will create greater swing speeds, allowing you to hit the ball further, even as you start to tune your swing. If you’re not a full-on beginner or aren’t looking for any extra distance, a set with steel shafts are a great choice. These will be easier to grow into skill-wise, making it easier to adapt as your game improves. As your swing speed improves, the flex of graphite shafts will be too much, and you’ll need to graduate to iron shafts then.

The main factors in forgiveness are club head and shaft. There’s a lot to dig into with this (we could write an entire essay on these two things), but in general, most beginner sets are outfitted with the absolute easiest club head to hit and a graphite shaft that allows for greater swing speed and fewer mistakes. We’d say not to get caught up in the nitty-gritty and focus on finding a set that is made for new players—something that almost every brand will outline in its product descriptions. Make sure you take a look to see what handicap each club set is designed for and pick the one made for high handicappers (that’s you), as these are coined as player improvement clubs.

According to recent reports, golf club prices run the gamut, but a good set of beginner clubs will usually run you anywhere from $250 to $1,000. This is a huge discrepancy, but there is a big range in quality from bottom to top. If you’re a brand-new golfer, spending $1,000 isn’t necessary, but if you think you’re in it for the long haul and want a set of sticks that are going to allow you to progress without having to upgrade, spending a little more cash is a great idea—the technology really does make a difference and it'll save you with an upgrade in a year or two if you improve.

To help facilitate the best golf club sets on the market in 2026, I consulted with Senior Gear and Commerce Editor Ryan Brower (a mid-handicapper himself) to determine which clubs available are truly worthwhile. We evaluated each on club head size, materials, shaft construction, and forgiveness. Some sets, like the Stix full setup, gave us the chance to see what a quality set of clubs can do for a high handicapper, while the more affordable sets gave us a good idea of what is possible at a low price point. Even for someone like me, who may only get on the links a couple of times a year, using any of the sets listed below can have an instant improvement in gameplay. Brower typically plays around 20 rounds per year, so he definitely knows his way around a course. Ultimately, we picked sets that we liked the most, but there are so many options today, you really can’t go wrong when you’re trying to make a decision, because, hey, you can always upgrade.

Beginners to golf do not need to get a custom fitting for clubs, but if you have the money and want to go all in on your new hobby, then we won't stop you. Really the main measurement you want to get right when buying is proper club sizing (not too tall or too short)—and the good news is most of these clubs will have a solid fit for just starting out.

Recent findings suggest that the only initial adjustments you need to make as a beginner are if you are exceptionally tall or short. If you are over 6'2" consider sizing a half-inch or more length adjustment on your clubs. You can also just opt for a set that has a "Tall" option available. If you are under 5'5", you'll likely want a half-inch decrease in length adjustment.

If you like to go by feel, swinging your friends’ clubs or talking to a pro at your local course will help confirm the sizing you need. As you progress in your game, sizing can be pinpointed down further to personalized club sizing, if you choose.

Recent findings suggest that there's nothing wrong with buying pre-owned clubs to serve as your first beginner set. There is a whole market online for really nice pre-owned clubs for a solid price on sites like Ebay and the golf brands' websites. Yet the downside is, you guessed it, they were somebody else's. There's wear and tear on them.

Sources indicate that instead of buying pre-owned, opt for fresh. A new set will give you the proper tools to get acclimated on the course and really give you the opportunity to learn the game. Golf is a lot about feel. Your clubs should be your best friend out on the course, not some raggedy set whose best days are long gone.

Buying a new set also gives you something to build off of. As you get better you'll want to make upgrades. Maybe you want a more precise sand wedge or a driver with more power? What you'll do next is swap out single clubs one at a time until you find a set that fits your game to a T.

15 Best Bedroom Lighting Ideas for a Relaxing Ambience (2026)

📅 08 Sep 2021 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When you’re trying to unwind at the end of a long day, turning on the “major light” is simply not the move.
  • The secret lies in layered lighting, which involves a series of soft illumination sources working together in concert: A bedside lamp provides focused task lighting for reading, while wall sconces free up valuable nightstand space and introduce a soft diffused glow.
  • Dimmable fixtures and warm white light bulbs can be especially transformational in bedrooms that also function as an office or a hangout space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you’re trying to unwind at the end of a long day, turning on the “major light” is simply not the move. The glare of a way-too-bright overhead light is not only unflattering but oftentimes overstimulating. It can make your otherwise cozy bedroom feel more like a department-store dressing room, leaving relaxation a little bit harder to come by. The right bedroom lighting, on the other hand, can bring a sense of warmth, atmosphere, and visual interest to the space where you spend some of your most cherished downtime.

The secret lies in layered lighting, which involves a series of soft illumination sources working together in concert: A bedside lamp provides focused task lighting for reading, while wall sconces free up valuable nightstand space and introduce a soft diffused glow. Floor lamps can brighten an otherwise neglected corner, and a beautiful chandelier or pendant light doubles as a bedroom’s focal point, even when the light is switched off.

Dimmable fixtures and warm white light bulbs can be especially transformational in bedrooms that also function as an office or a hangout space. Ahead, we’ve rounded up our favorite bedroom lighting ideas, including sculptural statement pieces, portable table lamps, and wall-mounted fixtures that usher in a sense of calm.

For a reading nook, a work-from-home space, or just a little warm white lighting, a floor lamp can show off your taste without sacrificing functionality. We’ve pulled two designer-favorite must-haves for those in the world of interior design.

Recent findings suggest that this 1960s model from Danish designer Mads Caprani hasn’t gone out of style since its release. The pleated shade, bentwood spine, and U-shaped cast-iron base make it one of the most easily recognized and iconic designs in floor lamps to this day. If you’re looking to make a statement about your style, this piece does just that—landing somewhere between studious and stylish, as in polo champion Nacho Figueras’s Florida home.

It has been revealed that another lamp for tastemakers, this design from Isamu Noguchi has made the rounds in many celebrity home tours from a minimalist Brooklyn brownstone to Troye Sivan’s modern Melbourne home. Commerce director Rachel Fletcher has previously named a Noguchi lamp one of her bedroom essentials. The reputation of Noguchi’s work and the unique style of his Akari lamps make this a design staple for anyone hoping to cultivate a modern bedroom.

Industry observers note that we love the look of dual table lamps to frame your bed and create a distinct visual space in your bedroom. It also allows your bed to feel like a conscious design choice instead of a strictly functional piece. We’re taking bedside lamp notes from this Portland home owned by the lead singer of The Shins and decorated by Jessica Helgerson. And, if you don’t want to do things matchy-matchy, any one of these lamps would look great solo too.

It has been revealed that we love this moody metallic option from Article for a midcentury look—and we named it one of our favorite bedside lamps after ample editor testing. At $149, the price is also right.

If you’re struggling to find a table lamp that plays well with others, this is a viable option from coastal core experts Serena & Lily. This comes in four beautiful shades, inspired by the Italian shoreline, and there’s even a touch of rattan for a beachy bedside table moment.

The Flos Bellhop table lamp is a great source of ambient light in this minimalist Barcelona bedroom.

A godsend for a bedroom with inconvenient outlets, these design-forward portable lamps bring both ambience and task lighting wherever you need them.

Recent findings suggest that another favorite of interior designers, the Flos Bellhop table lamp is a great source of ambient light in a minimalist setting. These super-portable LED lamps have four dimmer settings, are USB-compatible, and can last up to 24 hours on a single charge. And, if you love the simple glass shape, they’re also available as wall sconces for a stylish outdoor lighting moment.

You never know when you’ll need a little extra light, and the Poldina Pro can adapt to your ever-changing needs. The lamp pairs a petite silhouette with the clean lines of Italian minimalist design, making it a versatile fit for your nightstand, dresser, or reading nook. Without any unsightly wires to speak of, the lamp can appear as an intentional design choice just about anywhere. Its touch-sensitive dimmer lets you adjust the brightness and choose between three color temperatures.

According to recent reports, AD shopping writer Julia Harrison, who tested the Micro version, appreciates its versatility for desk work and kitchen prep alike. She notes that the lamp “blends shyly and seamlessly into all setups that require a little, but not too much, light.” With approximately 12 hours of battery life, it’s an especially convenient option for adding a little extra illumination wherever you need it.

Wall lighting brings a warm dimension to the design of your bedroom and provides great task lighting for a bedtime read. While we love table lamps on matching nightstands, wall sconces bring an added degree of intentionality in their design, as seen in Walton Goggins’s guest bedroom and Jennifer Garner’s kid’s bedroom.

Available in 24 colors and with flexible orientation, this wall sconce channels the fun throwback design sensibility of Portland-based Schoolhouse. Not relegated to the bedroom alone, these fixtures can bring vibrancy to any space—as is evident in the bathroom of this timeless, edgy Massachusetts home.

A visible mending detail modernizes a traditional style, so the pleated lampshade remains classic without being too precious. We love to imagine this lining a long entryway, or on either side of a tall headboard—the perfect lighting for bedtime pages.

Recent findings suggest that linen shades are classic for a reason: They soften the appearance of a light fixture, giving even the most straightforward silhouettes a dash of warmth and character. Quince’s Contemporary Sconce pairs crisp white linen shades with a streamlined steel frame, available in brass or black for two distinctly different looks. The brass finish befits a more traditional bedroom, while the black feels especially sharp juxtaposed against pale walls and minimalist decor. Choose a single or double configuration depending on your space, or install a matching pair on either side of the bed for a polished alternative to bedside table lamps.

If a flower could moonlight as a light fixture, it would probably look something like Soho Home’s Florie Wall Light. Inspired by the interiors of White City House, the members’ club in West London, the sculptural design features two gently curved layers of champagne-colored glass that resemble a tulip’s petals. A fluted, bubbled texture gives the glass an almost vintage quality, while the frosted finish diffuses the light into a soft, atmospheric glow. Even at just nine inches tall and nine inches wide, the fixture has enough personality to stand on its own, though opting for a pair to flank the bed would be an especially charming choice to imbue the space with a dash of romance.

Actress Laura Harrier hangs a bespoke pendant lamp in her bedroom.

According to recent reports, the wrong kind of flush mount can be an eyesore, and the right kind of pendant light can transform a space from tragic to tasteful. These picks from IKEA and Lumens are both contemporary yet classic, proving them a satisfying finishing touch that makes all the difference.

Industry observers note that IKEA brings an affordable yet still-elevated style to the lineup with this ubiquitous, rattan-like pendant (technically latticed bamboo) from Ilse Crawford. We love this style as much for dining room lighting as we do for bedroom lighting. Can’t decide which? Two will only cost you $140 total.

In a recent development, danish lighting design has a knack for making even the most practical objects feel like works of art. Case in point: the PH 5 Hanging Lamp. Its distinctive arrangement of overlapping shades creates a sculptural silhouette, with each layer directing and diffusing light. The three-shade system sends most of the illumination downward while allowing a softer glow to escape around the sides for ambient lighting. The result is a striking pendant that commands attention, even when it’s not turned on. The light would look especially beautiful suspended above a bedside table in place of a traditional lamp.

Supermodel Elsa Hosk incorporated a pink Tronchi chandelier, made of Murano glass, into her Latest York City bedroom.

Might some consider a chandelier too much for a bedroom? Yes, someone who needs to live a little. A chandelier brings a sense of occasion to every space it’s in, and your bedroom deserves no less. These picks bring elegance without overkill.

We love how supermodel Elsa Hosk incorporated a pink Tronchi chandelier made of Murano glass into her Latest York City bedroom, and you can find a similar pick on 1stDibs if you want to sleep in rose-colored bliss.

Often referred to as the “boob light,” this type of flush mount can get a bad rap, but West Elm has figured out how to make them shine. This contemporary ceiling light fixture is simple, aesthetic, and subtle.

Serena & Lily’s Capiz Scalloped Chandelier has the delicate charm of a seaside find, with a little extra glamour courtesy of its antique-gold framing. Each translucent capiz shell is individually hand-set, creating a softly scalloped silhouette that feels like a piece of jewelry for the ceiling. The natural variations in the shells’ shapes and opacity give the fixture a beautiful sense of movement. Light filters through the overlapping layers to cast a warm diffused glow, making it an especially lovely choice for a bedroom where atmosphere matters just as much as illumination.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for guidance when it comes to your bedroom lights, it’s key to keep a variety of factors in mind. Do you do a lot of reading in bed? Maybe table lamps should be your primary focus. Do you have enough fixtures to keep the space illuminated but not too bright? Perhaps a floor lamp or two will provide that glow for you. Are you spending most of your time winding down and heading to sleep? Try a night-light or string lights for ambience! And, of course, you’ll want multiple light sources to get the look (and the vibe) just right. But don’t fret, we’ve combed the AD home tour archives—and shopping lists—for the best bedroom lights around.

#201644. Latest Update: Why Sleep Consistency May Be the Missing Piece When It Comes to Heart Health

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1739 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Why Sleep Consistency May Be the Missing Piece When It Comes to Heart Health

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1739 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you probably already know that getting seven to nine hours of sleep each night is one of the best things you can do for your health and wellbeing.
  • As it turns out, your heart might not be too happy about that.
  • Before you start stressing over every late night or weekend sleep-in, though, there's some important context to understand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you probably already know that getting seven to nine hours of sleep each night is one of the best things you can do for your health and wellbeing. But what happens if you’re consistently hitting that goal while going to bed at different times? Think 10 p.m. on Monday, midnight on Wednesday, and well past 1 a.m. on Saturday because it’s the weekend, after all.

As it turns out, your heart might not be too happy about that. Upcoming research suggests that sleep consistency—which includes both when you go to bed and wake up, and how much sleep you get from night to night—could play an notable role in cardiovascular health. And, while getting the recommended amount of shut-eye still matters, researchers are finding that how much your sleep fluctuates may deserve some attention, too.

Before you start stressing over every late night or weekend sleep-in, though, there's some important context to understand. Here's what the research actually found, why your body seems to care so much about routine, and how consistent your sleep schedule really needs to be.

In a recent development, meet the experts: Nguyen Minh Tuan Viet, MD, PhD, is a neuroscientist and postdoctoral research fellow at Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School and lead researcher of the latest study. Nour Makarem, PhD, is a cardiovascular epidemiologist in the department of epidemiology at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health. Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, is a professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center.

For the new study published in Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, researchers analyzed more than one million nights of sleep data from 10,362 adults participating in the National Institutes of Health's All of Us Research Program, an initiative that aims to collect data from over one million Americans and create the country’s largest biomedical database.

Unlike previous studies that only looked at people's sleep habits for about a week, this one used about six months of Fitbit data to see how participants' bedtimes, wake-up times, and total sleep duration changed from night to night. They then compared those patterns with participants’ medical records and tracked their health for nearly four years.

The findings were pretty eye-opening: For every additional 29 minutes of variation in how long someone slept from night to night, their relative risk of serious heart problems, including heart attacks, heart failure, heart muscle disease, and certain strokes, was 24 percent higher. To be clear, that doesn't mean going to bed 29 minutes later than usual on a given night increases your heart disease risk by 24 percent. The researchers were looking at a statistical measure of how much someone's total sleep duration varied over time, rather than the consequences of one late bedtime. As of now, all this information does it point to a potential link between sleep schedule variation and heart disease.

According to recent reports, researchers also found that greater night-to-night fluctuations in bedtime and wake-up times were associated with a 23 percent and 20 percent higher relative risk of cardiovascular problems, respectively. This means that both the consistency of your sleep schedule and the consistency of the duration of that sleep may play a role in heart health.

There are a few things worth keeping in mind, though. For starters, this study found a connection between inconsistent sleep and heart problems, but it couldn't prove that irregular sleep is what causes those problems. In fact, Viet points out that the relationship could work in the opposite direction too (i.e. early illness might actually make someone’s sleep more irregular). Plus, most participants were women and white, so we can't necessarily assume the findings apply to everyone. Still, the results add to growing evidence that sleep consistency deserves a place in the heart-health conversation.

It has been revealed that your body has its own internal clock, known as your circadian rhythm, which determines when you're tired, when you're wide awake, and even how bodily functions like blood pressure and heart rate change throughout the day. And, it works at its best when it has a reasonably predictable schedule to follow. When you're constantly changing when you sleep and wake, you may disrupt that rhythm, a phenomenon known as circadian misalignment, explains Nour Makarem, PhD, a cardiovascular epidemiologist in the department of epidemiology at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health.

According to recent reports, that disruption can impact some pretty key cardiovascular processes, like how your body regulates blood pressure. Under normal circumstances, blood pressure usually drops by about 10 to 20 percent while you're sleeping to give your cardiovascular system a period of rest, but research by Makarem suggests that irregular sleep patterns may be associated with higher blood pressure and an increased risk of hypertension. “This is problematic because higher nocturnal blood pressure and having a non-dipping profile (blood pressure that does not dip or dip enough during sleep) are associated with higher risk for heart disease and stroke, the leading causes of death in women,” she indicates.

It has been revealed that your sleep schedule may also interact with other daily rhythms, including when you eat and exercise. These behaviors help regulate biological clocks throughout your body, including those involved in metabolism, Makarem notes. When those clocks fall out of sync, processes like blood sugar regulation may be affected, too. In fact, research has linked irregular sleep patterns with poorer glucose regulation and a higher risk of metabolic challenges.

Industry observers note that research is still emerging, but scientists are noticing some key links between sleep consistency and heart health. A 2025 study published in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health followed more than 72,000 adults and found that people with irregular sleep patterns had a higher risk of major cardiovascular events, including heart attacks and strokes. Another study published in Sleep in 2024 analyzed sleep patterns in more than 60,000 adults and found that sleep regularity was a stronger predictor of mortality risk than sleep duration in that population.

Recent findings suggest that so, does this mean having a consistent bed and rising time matters more than getting eight hours? Not necessarily. "The evidence for sleep regularity is rather nascent relative to that for sleep duration," indicates Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, a professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. She explains that while several studies have made the connection between irregular sleep and poorer health outcomes, more research needs to be done to determine whether making someone's sleep schedule more consistent can actually lower their cardiovascular risk. And, we do have plenty of evidence that getting enough sleep has positive affects on just about every system in the body, from brain function to muscle recovery.

Overall, there are still things researchers are learning about sleep consistency and heart health, but it’s safe to start thinking of it as another piece of the puzzle, alongside getting enough hours and making sure those hours are restorative.

Here's the million-dollar question: Does protecting your heart mean going to bed at exactly 10:30 p.m. every single night, no exceptions? Thankfully, no.

Ultimately, you’ve got some wiggle room. "In general, we would recommend that individuals try not to deviate by 60 min up or down from their average bedtime or sleep duration," says St-Onge, but the smaller the gap, the better.

According to recent reports, think of that as a target, not a hard-and-fast rule. An occasional late night or weekend sleep-in isn’t a reason to panic. What matters more is establishing a reasonably consistent pattern over a period of time rather than expecting yourself to follow a perfect schedule every single night.

Sources indicate that if you've had a particularly short night, St-Onge recommends trying to go to bed a little earlier and waking up a little later when your schedule allows, rather than trying to make up for all that lost sleep by sleeping in for hours. Most importantly, don't sweat it. "If one night is off, it's not all doom and gloom; you get right back on schedule the following night," notes St-Onge.

Here are a few small changes experts recommend to improve your sleep routine without completely overhauling your lifestyle.

Sources indicate that before committing to being in bed every night by 9 p.m., consider what will actually make sense for your schedule. Earlier isn't automatically better. What's important is getting adequate sleep on a schedule that works with your body's natural rhythm and everyday responsibilities, explains St-Onge.

If your current bedtime is midnight but you'd ideally like to be asleep by 11, there's no need to make that change all at once. Makarem recommends gradually shifting your bedtime earlier by about 10 minutes each day until you reach your target. The idea is to give your body time to adjust rather than suddenly expecting yourself to fall asleep an hour earlier than usual.

In a recent development, it's tempting to stay up late on Friday and Saturday nights and make up for it by sleeping well into the morning, but even those brief changes can leave you feeling out of sync by the time Monday rolls around. If possible, St-Onge recommends keeping your weekend bedtimes within about an hour of your usual routine.

If you wear an Apple Watch or Fitbit to bed, you know how easy it is to get caught up in the numbers. One morning you're celebrating a great sleep score, and the next you're wondering what went wrong because your tracker states you barely got any deep sleep.

Industry observers note that while these devices can be helpful for spotting patterns, the last thing you want is to start losing sleep over your sleep. Makarem recommends using trackers to keep tabs on your habits or remind you when it's time for bed, but only if they're actually helping. If checking your sleep stats is making you anxious, it's fine to ditch the data and simply pay attention to when you're going to bed and waking up.

And remember, you don't have to get your sleep schedule exactly right every single night to do something good for your heart. Small changes that you can actually stick with are worth more than chasing a perfect score. As Makarem puts it, "Progress is better than perfect.".

Why Living with Endometriosis May Double Your Odds of Migraine

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in a fresh analysis, researchers found females with endometriosis were 2.3 times more likely to also have migraine, and they noted the two conditions may share a pain pathway involving nerves and inflammation.Recognizing that connection earlier could lead to coordinated care for both conditions, the researchers said.The analysis, presented at the American Neurological Association (ANA) Annual Meeting in San Diego on October 20, included more than 13 million females.
  • It has been revealed that endometriosis occurs when tissue similar to what lines the uterus grows outside the uterus, Mallory Stuparich, MD, a gynecologic surgeon at MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, California, told Healthline.
  • In a recent development, stuparich stated endometriosis pain typically develops in 2 ways.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in a fresh analysis, researchers found females with endometriosis were 2.3 times more likely to also have migraine, and they noted the two conditions may share a pain pathway involving nerves and inflammation.Recognizing that connection earlier could lead to coordinated care for both conditions, the researchers said.The analysis, presented at the American Neurological Association (ANA) Annual Meeting in San Diego on October 20, included more than 13 million females. The research hasn’t yet been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

It has been revealed that endometriosis occurs when tissue similar to what lines the uterus grows outside the uterus, Mallory Stuparich, MD, a gynecologic surgeon at MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, California, told Healthline. Stuparich was not involved in the study.Yohannes Woubishet Woldeamanuel, MD, lead author of the study and assistant professor of neurology at Mayo Clinic Arizona, told Healthline that migraine also involves more than one part of the body.“Migraine is more than a headache,” he said.Headache is one symptom, Woldeamanuel said, but migraine can also cause sensory, motor, and balance symptoms.“Migraine is a little complex. It’s a multiple-nervous system involving a condition,” he said.

In a recent development, stuparich stated endometriosis pain typically develops in 2 ways. The first starts in the lesions themselves.“There are inflammatory markers that are created by the endometriosis lesions themselves, and those inflammatory markers can irritate the nerves that live close by the lesions,” she said.The second involves the nervous system, Stuparich said. Scar tissue can grow its own nerve supply, and years of chronic pain can change how the nervous system responds. That adaptation can “perpetuate pain or make people feel sensations that normally wouldn’t be painful,” she said.Stuparich said the inflammatory and immune processes involved in endometriosis have “pretty significant overlap in the setting of migraines.”.

One possible link between the two conditions is calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a chemical messenger that helps transmit pain signals, the researchers noted.CGRP plays a key role in migraine attacks, Woldeamanuel said, and blocking it reduces those attacks. CGRP medications work by blocking the sites where CGRP attaches or by binding to CGRP itself.Researchers have also found CGRP in endometriosis tissue.

In a recent development, A 2024 study published in Science Translational Medicine found CGRP in endometriosis lesions from both people and mice. In mice, blocking CGRP signaling reduced pain and reduced lesion size.

Other studies point to shared biology between the two conditions:.

According to recent reports, stuparich remarked she was “not surprised at all” by the finding because it matches what she sees in her own patients.“We see this overlap of patients who have endometriosis also having migraines,” she said.Stuparich said the science still has gaps. She noted that nothing has been proven conclusively in peer-reviewed research yet, but the way both diseases behave supports a connection.“It makes sense that there would be overlap,” she said.

Endometriosis and migraine are treated by different specialists, so the overlap is easy to miss, Woldeamanuel said.For the analysis, researchers at Mayo Clinic Arizona reviewed 35 studies published over 50 years, comparing migraine rates among 207,675 females with endometriosis and 12,963,120 females without the condition.Short-term health records miss up to 90% of that overlap, according to the analysis. Migraine rates in females with endometriosis changed depending on how each study identified migraine.“This data is hiding,” Woldeamanuel said.

Sources indicate that “These two clinics are siloed. One clinic doesn’t ask about the other condition. They just focus on their own specialty,” Woldeamanuel said.The findings of the analysis have not been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

It has been revealed that some treatments already overlap, Stuparich noted. Hormonal birth control “can sometimes be used to treat menstrually associated migraines,” she said.Stuparich said she has heard anecdotally of patients whose endometriosis symptoms improved after they started CGRP medications for migraine, though long-term data are still lacking.The researchers said the findings support studying whether existing CGRP-blocking migraine medications could also relieve endometriosis pain, potentially offering one treatment for both conditions.Woldeamanuel leads a planned Mayo Clinic trial testing one of those medications, rimegepant (Nurtec ODT), for endometriosis pain. The trial will also track migraine days in participants who have both conditions. It’s expected to finish in 2031, according to ClinicalTrials.gov.

It has been revealed that people who suspect they have both conditions can take steps now to get them treated together, Stuparich noted.Patients can raise the connection themselves, Stuparich said. She suggested a starting point for each appointment:.

Patients can also ask for an early referral to the other specialist so both conditions get coordinated care, Woldeamanuel said. “The earlier it’s diagnosed, the better it’s managed,” he said.Stuparich said doctors are moving away from viewing endometriosis as only a gynecologic disorder because it can affect the whole body.“It is a whole body systemic neuroinflammatory neuroimmune disorder,” she said.

#201641. Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (807 w)

Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume.
  • According to recent reports, whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation.
  • Industry observers note that to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume. Whale carcasses will sink to the bottom and become marine life habitats. Whale pee nourishes the entire ocean. But how about whale snot? The microbes and other biological material emitted from their blowholes when the giant cetaceans breathe has helped scientists sequence an entire whale genome: Take that whale vomit. The findings are detailed in a study published today in the journal Molecular Ecology Resources.

According to recent reports, whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation. With genomic data, researchers can measure population health, to see how much genetic diversity and inbreeding is present. It can also help identify individual animals for monitoring, help determine an animal’s sex, and estimate the population’s size.

Industry observers note that to obtain genetic data from whales, marine biologists historically have had to conduct a skin biopsy. They’ll take a dart, stick it into the whale’s blubber, and take a small sample of the skin and blubber. However, during sampling, boats must get close to the whales, which can disturb them. In some locations and for some endangered species, getting close enough to take a biopsy isn’t permitted or possible.

Sources indicate that that’s where whale snot—or blow—comes in. For this study, a team from Scotland’s University of St. Andrews, the University of Copenhagen in Denmark, the North Coast Cetacean Society, and Fisheries and Oceans Canada used several small drones off the coast of British Columbia. The drones were equipped with sterile petri dishes to collect the samples.

The team flew the drone through the exhaled breaths of one North pacific humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae kuzira) at a time, but still sampled several individual whales. The humpbacks generally took one to six breaths every time they surfaced—covering the drone and the dishes in whale snot.

According to recent reports, the team collected 58 blow samples from 26 individual humpback whales. They also took repeated samples from the same whales, collected in different encounters and across two years to match the genomes. They then cross-referenced the genomes collected from the whale blow with genomes sequenced from traditional blubber biopsies taken from the same animals.

Industry observers note that to keep the DNA from mixing, the team targeted the whale most upwind in the pod, since the blow downwind might mix with the blow from the whales up ahead. Resting whales were never sampled, and the team stopped the drone flights if a whale showed any reaction. More than one third of samples were collected by flying the drone directly from land—no boat required.

Industry observers note that the DNA was sequenced to produce two types of genomes. Low-coverage nuclear genomes, which are inherited from both parents, and high-coverage mitochondrial genomes, which are inherited from the mother only.

The team found that the genetic diversity estimated from the blow samples was very similar to the estimates taken from traditional biopsies. Fortunately, the humpback population in the study shows little evidence of recent inbreeding. There is a small proportion of the genome that has long stretches of identical DNA, but the team believes that most likely reflects distant shared ancestry or past population bottlenecks.

Sources indicate that according to the team, this research marks one of the first whole genome datasets for a group of North Pacific humpback whales. Previously, only one North Pacific humpback whole genome was publicly available.

“We will use these blow-derived genomes to not only assess population structure and health, but also assess kinship and family ties among humpback whales foraging in northern British Columbia,” Dr. Éadin O’Mahony, a study co-author and marine mammal ecologist who was at the University of St. Andrews at the time of the study, remarked in a statement. “The aim is to understand how their social bonds form: Are the whales that forage together family, or long-term friends?”.

Sources indicate that as expected, the North Pacific humpback whales were genetically distinct from their counterparts living in the North Atlantic. This confirms that data taken from whale blow works as well from data taken from conventional biopsies. The drone-captured genetic analyses also correctly determined every whale’s sex, and revealed three previously undescribed mitochondrial DNA variants, which could help show how some of these whales are related. The blow from whales swimming in groups also did not have any sign of contamination from neighboring whales.

About 16 percent of the DNA in each blow sample were also primarily from the microbes living in the whale’s airways. According to the team, this indicates that a single breath could tell us about the individual whale and its respiratory microbiome, opening up a potential upcoming window into cetacean health.

That’s a whole lot of data from just a little bit of snot.

What Is the Best Type of Yogurt? We Narrowed It Down to the World’s 8 Healthiest.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Okay, maybe not everyone, but there's a reason yogurt has been a dietary staple in dozens of countries for centuries.
  • "Most of the world is lactose intolerant and has been for thousands and thousands of years," states Robert Hutkins, PhD, a professor of food microbiology at the University of Nebraska.
  • Whether you need help digesting lactose or not, the latest research suggests that yogurt has wide-ranging benefits, from enhancing gut health to improving blood sugar control to maybe even reducing your risk of an early death.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EVERYBODY LOVE YOGURT. Okay, maybe not everyone, but there's a reason yogurt has been a dietary staple in dozens of countries for centuries. Yogurt doesn't spoil as fast as milk, yet still delivers milk's nutrients—protein, calcium, potassium, magnesium—without the same risk of, um, certain GI issues.

"Most of the world is lactose intolerant and has been for thousands and thousands of years," states Robert Hutkins, PhD, a professor of food microbiology at the University of Nebraska. "Humans figured out that even if they were lactose intolerant, they could still consume cultured milks because the culture helps degrade the lactose before it gets to the colon and gets fermented by gas-producing microbes.".

Whether you need help digesting lactose or not, the latest research suggests that yogurt has wide-ranging benefits, from enhancing gut health to improving blood sugar control to maybe even reducing your risk of an early death.

From Europe to Asia to Africa, all yogurt starts with the same basic ingredients: milk and good bacteria. But no two types are exactly alike. Here's what to know before your next grocery run.

Traditional Greek yogurt is strained through a cheesecloth to remove excess fluid. Yogurt factories use centrifuges or special filters instead. What's left behind is a thick, smooth yogurt with a slightly acidic flavor and a concentrated source of nutrients, including about 18 grams of protein per 6-ounce container.

In a recent development, some food makers add thickeners as a shortcut, so check the label for a simple ingredient list of milk, cream, and yogurt cultures. "The products with thickeners added have a different texture, a little bit more gumminess," indicates Molly Kimball, RD, CSSD, a dietitian based in Louisiana. Swap in Greek yogurt for sour cream or mayo, or stir it into guacamole—the lactic acid slows down the oxidation that turns avocados brown.

Recent findings suggest that technically considered a soft cheese, skyr is strained like Greek yogurt to produce something firm yet creamy. It's usually made with skim milk, yielding yogurt with slightly more protein than Greek yogurt: about 19 grams of protein per 6 ounces. Use skyr to make dips hearty enough to stand up to cut vegetables (or chips). Or stir it into bolognese to impart a velvety texture and an extra boost of protein.

According to recent reports, this yogurt variety isn't strained, so it has a thinner texture and less protein than its Greek or Icelandic cousins: about 6 grams per 6 ounces. Traditional Bulgarian yogurt gets its signature sharp flavor from high concentrations of the aptly named Lactobacillus Bulgaricus bacteria, which produce lactic acid. Kimball recommends blending Bulgarian yogurt into smoothies to add a tanginess that counterbalances sweeter ingredients.

Most yogurts are fermented in large vats. As yogurt bacteria digest milk, they produce a wide variety of metabolites, including gel-like substances called exopolysaccharides. Then the yogurt is pumped into the smaller containers we snag at the grocery store.

With French-style yogurt, the milk and bacterial cultures are poured into cups earlier, before the microbes multiply. "That gives you a more custardy product because it hasn't gone through this pumping phase that disturbs the gel," says Hutkins. Inside a 6-ounce cup of French-style yogurt, you'll find about 5 grams of protein. To try it the French way, eat your yogurt for dessert, alone or paired with a little honey or jam.

This tangy, thin, pourable yogurt is fermented with kefir grains–gelatinous clusters that contain milk proteins and up to 50 bacterial and yeast species. During fermentation, these yeasts can leave behind traces of alcohol and carbon dioxide, or fizz. However, many mass-produced kefirs use standardized starter cultures instead to maintain consistent product quality and keep the alcohol concentration low enough to sell in grocery stores.

Kimball suggests drinking plain kefir, Russian or otherwise. It packs about 8 grams of protein per cup. If you can't handle the sour flavor, balance it with a teaspoon or less of maple syrup or a few drops of stevia or monk fruit. If you want a flavored variety, pick one with no more than 5 grams of added sugar.

Industry observers note that sweet and mildly acidic, dahi is the key ingredient in Indian staples like lassi–a yogurt drink often flavored with mango, spices, or rosewater–and raita, the sauce that cools your mouth when you order your vindaloo extra hot. Some dahi varieties contain Leuconostoc, bacteria that produce a metabolite called diacetyl that imparts a buttery flavor. Each six-ounce serving of dahi packs about 7 grams of protein.

It has been revealed that drinkable like kefir, laban is sour but smooth and contains about 5 grams of protein per six ounces. Strain it in a colander or cheesecloth to make labneh, a thick, soft, yogurt-like cheese traditionally smeared on sandwiches and stacked on mezze platters.

Sources indicate that this drinkable yogurt is often thicker than fermented milk beverages. Its mix of cultures, which hail mostly from the Lactobacillusgenus, imparts a moderately acidic flavor with subtle buttery notes. Amasi packs about 6 grams of protein per six ounces. It's traditionally eaten with maize or sorghum porridge, especially at breakfast.

Julie Stewart is a writer and content strategist whose work has also appeared in Health, and Women’s Health, Everyday Health, Vice, and Shape.
